sentences.text: The meeting was held to prepare for a hearing on 15 December and to review the local authority's letter.
Solicitor Priya Mehta attended as the solicitor.
Client Kerry Dobson attended as the client.
The client described contact with Tyler as occurring Tuesdays and Thursdays at the family centre on Mill Lane.
The client reported that Tyler keeps asking when he can come home.
The client reported that a worker described the contact period as 'warm'.
The client reported that Tyler lost his front tooth.
The client reported that Tyler likes the foster carers and that they have a dog.
The client reported that Tyler is still at Ashgrove Primary.
The client reported that the foster carers drive Tyler to school and that his teacher says he is doing better with reading.
The client disclosed that they had used crack last weekend.
The client stated that the crack use was 'just the once' and later retracted this statement, saying 'forget I said that' and claiming it was 'nothing' and they were 'clean'.
The client stated that they had used crack on Saturday night at their cousin's flat.
The client disclosed that they had been using heroin since 3 November.
The client reported that they use heroin every day by smoking it, not injecting.
The client reported that the cost of heroin is about £40 a day.
The client stated that they pay for heroin using their Universal Credit and by borrowing from their nan, who believes the money is for gas.
The client reported that they stopped picking up their script about three weeks ago.
The client confirmed they live at the flat on Corporation Street and that rent is paid directly.
The client reported that they are behind on council tax.
The client reported that they have a naloxone kit somewhere but it is probably out of date.
The client stated their primary objective is for Tyler to come home.
The client asked if contact would be stopped if the hair-strand test came back positive.
The solicitor stated that a hair test usually covers about three months and that the client's disclosed use is likely to show up.
The solicitor advised that it is better for the client to tell the social worker before the test result if they are already back in treatment, as this looks different to the court.
The solicitor stated that courts do not usually stop contact over a relapse alone if the client is turning up sober and engaging, but noted that hiding it is what worries the court
The solicitor stated that the client cannot file a statement saying they are clean.
The solicitor disclosed that the risk of overdose is highest when going back to heroin after a break.
The solicitor advised the client to get a new naloxone kit from the Recovery Hub, which will provide one the same day.
The solicitor instructed the client to ring the Harbridge Recovery Hub to restart their script by Friday 27.
